speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having a psychiatric condition and a new onset movement disorder; could you describe exactly what movements you are experiencing and when they started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful background. To evaluate your movement disorder, are these involuntary movements more noticeable when you are trying to do something (dyskinesia) or do they occur at rest (chorea/tremor)? Also, have you noticed any stiffness, shaking, or slowed movement in your body?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms you describe—persistent restlessness, fidgeting, and an inability to remain still—are classic signs of akathisia. Given your recent initiation of risperidone, this is a likely side effect. Have you noticed any muscle stiffness, tremors, or changes in your handwriting as well?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced Akathisia secondary to Risperidone.

The symptoms of inner restlessness, fidgeting, and an inability to sit still you are describing, occurring two months after starting risperidone, are classic signs of akathisia. Since your psychiatric symptoms are improving, we should not stop the medication, but we will adjust the dose or add a beta-blocker to manage this side effect. Are you currently experiencing any difficulty sleeping due to this restlessness?
